content: Doxycycline is a broad-spectrum antibiotic that is synthetically derived from oxytetracycline. Doxycycline Monohydrate Capsules are available in strengths of 100 mg, 75 mg, and 50 mg, containing doxycycline monohydrate equivalent to 100 mg, 75 mg, or 50 mg of doxycycline, respectively, for oral administration. The chemical designation of doxycycline, which appears as a light-yellow crystalline powder, is alpha-6-deoxy-5-oxytetracycline. Doxycycline exhibits a high degree of lipid solubility and a low affinity for calcium binding. It is highly stable in normal human serum and does not degrade into an epianhydro form. The inactive ingredients in the capsules include colloidal silicon dioxide, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and sodium starch glycolate. The capsules themselves are made of hard gelatin and contain colorants. For the 100 mg and 75 mg strengths, the capsule shell includes black iron oxide, red iron oxide, titanium dioxide, and yellow iron oxide. For the 50 mg strength, the shell contains titanium dioxide and yellow iron oxide. The capsules are printed with edible ink. For the 50 mg and 100 mg strengths, the ink contains black iron oxide, red iron oxide, and yellow iron oxide. For the 75 mg strength, the ink contains black iron oxide, FD&C Blue No. 2, FD&C Red No. 40, FD&C Blue No. 1, and D&C Yellow No. 10.
